book.title: 1934: Caught in the Crossroads
book.tagline: A relic from the Crusades resurfaces, threatening a world already on the brink.
description: March 1934. The True Cross has been lost since the Crusades. It's about to resurface at the worst possible time.

Routine railway work in Yugoslavia uncovers a sealed basement: the remains of Ottoman soldiers trapped since the Siege of Vienna, and documents lost for two hundred and fifty years. They include the Grand Vizier's campaign inventory. One item doesn't belong.
The unveiling in Ljubljana's museum ends with the ledger stolen, two men unconscious, and the police taking statements from four people who had no idea why it mattered to Berlin.

Standing in their way, almost by accident, are a company security chief summoned by a vague telegram, his actress sister, who jumps to conclusions as easily as she reads a room, an archaeologist entangled in the kind of mess he has spent his career trying to avoid, and a German scholar who lost everything when she said the wrong thing out loud.
None of them could do it alone. They lack authority and support, but if they do nothing, no one else will.

They follow the trail east: a stripped excavation on the Drava, a chapel in Vienna under martial law, the Orient Express, a monastery on an island in Romania. They make it up as they go across a continent sliding toward darkness.
It is 1934, and the worst still feels avoidable.
For readers wanting competent people who are not invincible, plans that fail, and a villain too clever for either side's good.
